observation.visible_scene: A hazy, fog-overcast sky seen through dense mist. A faint pale circular halo (a ring around a dim, slightly bluish center) sits on the left mid-frame throughout. A darker cloud bank runs across the top edge with a small blue-sky gap near the upper center, and a brownish-gray fog/cloud layer fills the lower half of the frame.
visible_changes: The left-side halo stays at a nearly constant image position across all frames, but its visibility fluctuates: it is clearer in some frames (e.g. around t=0.13, 0.27, 1.60, 1.80, 2.00) and fainter or washed out in others (e.g. t=1.00-1.27).

The upper cloud bank slowly drifts/reshapes: the blue-sky region at the top-right becomes progressively more exposed from the middle of the excerpt onward, while the dark cloud band above shifts slightly.
The lower fog/cloud texture morphs and shifts subtly, with the brownish cloud masses at the bottom changing shape and position over time.
Overall brightness and contrast of the foggy layer vary gently frame to frame, consistent with thin, moving mist.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the halo is a sun corona seen through fog or a lens artifact, and what is occluded behind the mist.
The cause and later evolution of the fog/cloud drift, which are not shown within this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain: the stable position of the left halo suggests little camera translation, but the changing top cloud bank could be either cloud drift or slow camera pan/rotation; the background evidence is insufficient to separate the two with confidence.
The apparent flickering of the halo is hard to attribute definitively to fog density changes versus exposure/compression variation.
